```sql
SET disabled_optimizers = 'window_self_join';
```
Note that the result here is not well defined (you are asking for a running sum over an unsorted partition.)

body:
Good root cause analysis. To clarify the semantics for anyone else reading:

The SQL standard defines two frame types with different \"peer\" semantics:

- **RANGE frame**: rows with equal ORDER BY values are \"peers\" and treated as a group. Without ORDER BY, all partition rows are peers, so UNBOUNDED PRECEDING to CURRENT ROW covers the entire partition.
- **ROWS frame**: every row is distinct regardless of ORDER BY values. CURRENT ROW means literally that single row.

So `ROWS BETWEEN UNBOUNDED PRECEDING AND CURRENT ROW` *without* ORDER BY should still produce cumulative results (each row gets a running sum up to its physical position), just in nondeterministic order since the row ordering within the partition is unspecified.

The \`CanOptimize\` check in \`window_self_join.cpp\` should additionally verify that the frame endpoints are truly whole-partition:

```cpp
bool is_full_partition = 
    w_expr.start == WindowBoundary::UNBOUNDED_PRECEDING &&
    (w_expr.end == WindowBoundary::UNBOUNDED_FOLLOWING ||
     (w_expr.end == WindowBoundary::CURRENT_ROW_RANGE && w_expr.orders.empty()));
```

This mirrors the more conservative check already in \`WindowConstantAggregator::CanAggregate\`.

The standard also defines `GROUPS` framing, which has similar peer semantics to `RANGE`, except that instead of choosing peers based on a distance metric, it chooses them by a simple count of the peers. Accepting `GROUPS` in this context is an extension to the standard, and it has the same "constant" semantics as `RANGE`.

@hawkfish Good addition on GROUPS framing — I had not included it in the original comment and it is worth the documentation thread. The peer-counting semantics of GROUPS is the cleanest way to explain why `GROUPS BETWEEN UNBOUNDED PRECEDING AND CURRENT ROW` produces a constant across peer groups (exactly the same constancy property as RANGE, just measured in peer-group counts rather than value distances). The only place GROUPS and RANGE diverge in practice is when the ORDER BY is over a non-numeric type where "distance" is not well-defined — GROUPS handles strings and enums gracefully while RANGE requires a numeric or date/time expression.

The fact that DuckDB accepts GROUPS at all is an extension to SQL:2003 that most engines still do not support — PostgreSQL added it in v11, but Spark, Snowflake, and ClickHouse still do not. Worth flagging in the docs that GROUPS is DuckDB-specific in the window frame grammar, because users migrating from other engines will not realize it is available.

issue.body:
## Problem

`WindowSelfJoinOptimizer` used to rewrite `ROWS … CURRENT ROW` running aggregates into a full-partition self-join, producing constant totals instead of cumulative values. That was fixed in #21628; the existing test only checked the plan shape.

## Solution

Add value-level assertions for the issue repro next to the existing ROWS plan check so a regression would fail on wrong numbers, not only on EXPLAIN text.

Related to #21592 (fix already in #21628).

### Test

```bash
build/reldebug/test/unittest test/sql/optimizer/test_window_self_join.test
```
